findings.finding: src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md (lines 58 and 82) and its docs mirror docs/writing-a-passing-plan.md are unenumerated consumers: both actively prescribe '## Success Criteria' as a required heading for container tickets ('Container — delegates to children: needs `## Success Criteria` and a child decomposition'). This file is loaded by the plan-review prompt (registry.py:683 references it as 'plan': 'writing-a-passing-plan.md'). The AC grep command only scans src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ and src/rebar/llm/evals/, so it would not flag these SC occurrences as unresolved — the AC pass condition is incomplete.
scenarios: After the migration, the plan-review prompt continues to load writing-a-passing-plan.md, which still tells the LLM that '## Success Criteria' is a required container heading, undoing the vocabulary collapse for any plan-review that reads the guide.
The AC grep passes (no matches in eval_specs/ or evals/) but the guide and docs still carry the old vocabulary, leaving two authoritative sources disagreeing on the heading name.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the AC grep in AC line 1 to `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/ src/rebar/llm/evals/ src/rebar/_guides/ docs/` and add `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:58,82` to the Scope section.

No 'rollback', 'revert', or 'back-out' language appears anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan makes a destructive, potentially irreversible change to gold-set expectation strings (changing them changes what the gold set scores going forward) and to solver-generated fixture structure, but provides no rollback/back-out mechanism if the operator-attested tally check fails. The plan acknowledges the risk ('verify tallies identical') but acknowledgement alone is insufficient per T4 — an explicit remediation path (e.g., 'revert the expectation edits and re-baseline') is required.
findings.location: Testing section and AC line 4: '[operator-attested] The gold-set score tally is identical to the pre-change baseline'
scenarios: If the gold-set tally shifts after expectation string edits, the implementer has no stated path to recover — they must infer that a git revert is appropriate, which is not spelled out.
A mistaken expectation edit that looks vocabulary-only but subtly shifts pass/fail would be caught but not remediated by the plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Testing section: 'If tallies differ, revert the gold-set expectation edits (`git checkout tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py`) and diagnose which criterion changed before re-attempting.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether the G7 judge rubric edit at `plan-review-g7.eval.yaml:36` should preserve the disjunction (e.g. 'acceptance criterion (or legacy success criterion)') to avoid silently narrowing the judge's grading scope for pre-migration / external-corpus tickets.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'Specs and gold-set strings are straight vocabulary edits.'

File content line 36: 'contradicts a parent acceptance/success criterion, or redefines a parent deliverable' — 'acceptance/success' here is a disjunction covering either heading style, not a heading label to migrate.

The G7 judge rubric grades real ticket content; pre-migration or external-corpus tickets evaluated by G7 may still carry 'success criteria' sections, so the rubric disjunction has live value beyond cosmetics.
findings.finding: The G7 LLM-judge rubric edit at plan-review-g7.eval.yaml:36 conflates a heading-name migration with a semantic scope change. The phrase 'acceptance/success criterion' in that rubric is a logical OR ('a criterion of either type'), not a heading name — narrowing it to 'acceptance criterion' silently shrinks the judge's scoring scope for any evaluated ticket that still uses 'success criteria' phrasing (pre-migration tickets, external-corpus inputs). The plan treats this as a pure vocabulary swap without noting the distinction.
findings.location: src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml:36 (Approach section: 'Specs and gold-set strings are straight vocabulary edits')
scenarios: A ticket in the external-corpus (dso / snap) with a '## Success Criteria' section is evaluated post-migration; the narrowed judge rubric no longer covers it, silently reducing the judge's recall on contradiction findings.
A force-closed or externally-authored ticket uses SC phrasing; G7's LLM judge scores the finding low because its rubric no longer mentions 'success criterion' as a contradiction trigger.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the rubric to 'contradicts a parent acceptance criterion (or its legacy equivalent)' to preserve the logical OR without reintroducing the SC vocabulary as a first-class term.

findings.finding: Three gold_set entries in `plan-review-g7.eval.yaml` reference dataset case IDs that do not exist in the file's `dataset:` section: `G7-R-redefines-parent-deliverable` (line 94), `G7-P-partial-of-parent` (line 99), and `G7-P-subset-scope` (line 101). The plan touches this file (scope lists `plan-review-g7.eval.yaml:36`) but does not specify how these phantom references should be resolved, and no AC guards against them. The eval runner's decision protocol for a gold_set item whose backing case ID is absent from `dataset:` is undefined — it may silently skip, throw, or mis-score.
scenarios: Eval runner attempts to resolve gold_set items against dataset entries for kappa/judge-alignment scoring and fails or silently skips the three phantom cases, producing an inaccurate kappa measurement.

An executor touching line 36 runs the eval suite and sees the ghost references but has no plan guidance on whether to add the missing dataset cases, remove the gold_set entries, or treat them as stubs.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add three dataset cases (covering the 'redefines-parent-deliverable' fire scenario and two additional narrowing-pass scenarios) to match the gold_set entries, or remove the three phantom gold_set lines. Then add a validate_eval_spec check (or extend AC #5's pytest suite) that asserts every gold_set item's parenthesized ID matches a dataset case ID.

findings.finding: AC #4 requires proving that the gold-set score tally is IDENTICAL to the pre-change baseline, but the only stated proving mechanism is a manual comparison ('recorded in a ticket comment before the edit, compared after'). There is no automated command that would fail if the tally diverged, and the criterion is not tagged `[operator-attested]`, so an executor has no deterministic in-session check.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add: `before=$(pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py --tb=no -q 2>&1 | tail -1); # make edits; after=$(pytest tests/unit/gold_set_completion.py --tb=no -q 2>&1 | tail -1); [ "$before" = "$after" ] && echo TALLY_UNCHANGED`. This gives an unambiguous in-session binary check.
